clue.text: Bulletin from channel framing health centre

indicators.note: a frame goes round a picture, so the channel word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a ditch is a channel dug for water
a spa is a resort visited for health treatments

explanation.surface: A news report sent from the English Channel area about a clinic there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'channel' suggests the sea between England and France, but it is a humble ditch; 'framing' puts the spa inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispatch is an official report or news story sent in, as from a war correspondent.

clue.text: Keenly awaiting release of a poem by PhD in translation

indicators.note: translating turns words into new ones, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctoral graduate eagerly awaits the publication of a translated poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'release' sounds like publication; it is discharge from the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Demob-happy describes the elation of someone about to be demobilised or released from duty.

clue.text: Guy briefly retained by Touchstone to keep watch

indicators.note: the outer word retains the other by holding it within

parts.note: a touchstone is a standard against which things are judged

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: guy is taken as the word itself, then shortened

explanation.surface: A man is kept on by Shakespeare's jester Touchstone to stay on lookout.
explanation.walkthrough: Touchstone is the jester in As You Like It, but here a touchstone is a STANDARD, which holds GU.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand guard is to act as a sentry, keeping watch over something.

clue.text: Follow a century with another

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a ton is slang for a hundred, another century

explanation.surface: A cricketer's advice to follow one hundred with a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a century is a hundred runs, and a ton is the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To act on advice is to follow it, carrying out what it says.

clue.text: All there is beneath fertiliser staff dug in

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece beneath another follows it
the staff are dug into the fertiliser, going inside it

parts.note: compost is used to fertilise soil
men are staff or workers

explanation.surface: A gardener's whole workforce has dug compost into the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like a stick but means workers; 'dug in' places them before the fertiliser's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Compos mentis means of sound mind, which is what all there means informally.

clue.text: Scratch cricket side on call

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: to cry is to call out
the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A scratch cricket team turns up on the strength of a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratch' looks like an adjective for an improvised team, but here it is the verb: to withdraw from a contest. The OFF side is the half of a cricket field facing the batsman's bat.
explanation.definitionFit: To scratch from a race and to cry off both mean to withdraw from a commitment.

clue.text: Potential source of wealth in new normality?

indicators.note: new letters are a fresh arrangement of the old ones

explanation.surface: A question of whether the post-crisis new normal could make people rich.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Mint makes Britain's coins, so it literally produces money.

clue.text: I blundered, needing ultimately to go up backwards

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so each word gives its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone admits a mistake: they must eventually climb back up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' suggests a reversal, but it simply supplies its last letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: Oops is an exclamation one makes on realising a mistake, so it stands for an admission of error.

clue.text: Feature, primarily pretence or reality?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: an act is a pretence put on

explanation.surface: A question about whether a newspaper feature is mainly fiction or truth.
explanation.definitionFit: A fact is something true, part of reality rather than invention.

clue.text: Against cutting identical notes for the present

indicators.note: one piece cuts into the other, so it sits inside it

parts.note: ME (or MI) is a note of the sol-fa scale, so two identical notes give it twice
anti means against

explanation.surface: Someone opposes slicing through two matching banknotes, at least for now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests money, but these are sol-fa notes, the same one twice.
explanation.definitionFit: For the meantime and for the present are interchangeable ways of saying for now.

clue.text: Nutmeg's theme initially missed, showing lack of perception

parts.note: Nutmeg is the setter, so the setter's is MY

indicators.note: the theme word loses its opening letter, the one that comes initially

parts.note: a topic is a theme or subject

explanation.surface: The setter Nutmeg admits to overlooking a puzzle's theme, which shows obtuseness.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters refer to themselves by their pseudonym, so 'Nutmeg's' means MY. TOPIC loses its T to give OPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopic means short-sighted, and figuratively lacking foresight or insight.

clue.text: Wouldn't part with sole weapon that's proved trustworthy

parts.note: kept means held on to, not parted with
one means sole or single
a sword is a weapon

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to give up their only weapon, which has proved reliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who kept their word honoured a promise, showing themselves reliable.

clue.text: Youth leader's clanger, shielding internee at port

indicators.note: the outer word shields what it holds by wrapping round it

parts.note: a bell is something that clangs
Aden is a port in Yemen
POW, prisoner of war, is someone interned

explanation.surface: A youth leader commits a blunder while protecting a detainee at a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clanger' is British slang for a blunder, but here it is literally something that clangs; the port comes before the internee inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Baden-Powell founded the Scout movement, so he is the archetypal leader of young people.

clue.text: Work slicing sausages for game participants

indicators.note: the work cuts into the sausages, going inside them

parts.note: a polony is a type of cooked sausage
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A job of cutting up sausages for the players in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: A polony is a smooth pork sausage sold in Britain; the work slices it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo ponies are the horses ridden in polo matches, so they take part in the game.

clue.text: Kind person like Vlad once a Guardian worker?

parts.note: type means kind or sort
Vlad is a Guardian crossword setter

explanation.surface: Is a person like Vlad the Impaler ever kind? A Guardian reader wonders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vlad' calls up Vlad the Impaler, but he is a fellow Guardian crossword setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Typesetters arranged type for printing, a job at newspapers like the Guardian before computers.

clue.text: Drastic reduction in sales oddly overlooked

indicators.note: the reduction word goes into the letters that remain
the odd-numbered letters of sales are skipped, leaving the even ones

parts.note: a cut is a reduction

explanation.surface: A shop's sales are cut so sharply that the odd figures are ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly overlooked' leaves the even letters of sales, A and E, and CUT goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute problem is severe or critical, as a drastic situation is.

clue.text: Virtual trade exhibition shortly visiting London suburb

indicators.note: a visitor goes into a place, so this piece goes inside the suburb

parts.note: Epping is a town on the edge of London

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: a show is an exhibition

explanation.surface: An online trade fair, briefly passing through a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Epping is an Essex town at the end of a London Underground line; SHO goes after its E.
explanation.definitionFit: E-shopping is buying online, commerce carried out virtually rather than in a store.

clue.text: Union to scale down working during month

indicators.note: these pieces come during the month, inside its letters

parts.note: May is a month
to trim is to cut back or reduce
on means working or operating

explanation.surface: A trade union plans to cut back operations in the course of one month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' reads like a trade union but means marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Matrimony is the state of marriage, a union of two people.

clue.text: Leave layer covering ancient temple

parts.note: to part is to leave or depart
a hen is a bird that lays eggs
on can mean on top of, covering

explanation.surface: Instructions to remove a layer that is covering an old temple's stonework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' looks like a stratum but is an egg-layer, HEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parthenon is the temple of Athena on the Acropolis in Athens, built in classical antiquity.

clue.text: Some specified article plugged by seaman

indicators.note: a plug fills a gap, so the seaman goes into the article

parts.note: the is the definite article
OS, ordinary seaman, is a naval rank

explanation.surface: A news article is promoted by a particular sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: OS stands for ordinary seaman; it goes inside THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Those picks out particular people or things already identified, a specified group.

clue.text: Place for father to hide heiress, with plot brewing

indicators.note: something brewing is being mixed up, so these letters are stirred together

explanation.surface: A father seeks somewhere to conceal his heiress daughter while a conspiracy brews.
explanation.walkthrough: 'father' reads as a parent, but the father is a Catholic priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Priest holes were secret chambers in English houses where Catholic priests hid during persecution.

clue.text: This lady's going to Hull

parts.note: this lady is she, with the apostrophe running into the next words
'll, short for will, means going to

explanation.surface: A woman announces she is travelling to the Yorkshire city of Hull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hull' looks like the city in Yorkshire but means a casing; SHE'LL is she will, she is going to.
explanation.definitionFit: A hull or shell is the outer case of a seed or nut, or a ship's frame.

clue.text: Pilfer item from nativity scene

definitions.meaning: the manger in which the baby Jesus lay

explanation.surface: Someone steals a piece from a Christmas crib display.
explanation.definitionFit: Crib means both to steal in a small way and the manger shown in nativity scenes.

clue.text: Scheme taken up by venal politician

indicators.note: taken up says the hidden letters are read backwards
by here means held within the words that follow, so the answer sits among them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A plot adopted by a corrupt politician.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'taken up' means read upwards; NALP spans venal and politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan and a scheme are both arrangements worked out in advance.

clue.text: Caller from US contrarily set out for another meal

indicators.note: contrarily means the other way round, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: dialer is the American spelling of dialler, one who places a call

explanation.surface: An American visitor perversely lays the table for a second sitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caller' is a telephone caller, a DIALER in American spelling; read backwards it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A table relaid has had its cutlery and plates put out again for a further sitting.

clue.text: Person writing schedule substitutes second half of month

indicators.note: the schedule word takes the place of the latter four letters of the month

parts.note: November is a month
a list is a schedule

explanation.surface: Someone drafting a timetable swaps the later dates in a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second half of month' is the last four letters of the eleventh month, which the schedule word replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelist is an author of fiction, someone who writes for a living.

clue.text: Propitious start for government in African country

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the country's name

parts.note: Benin is a country in West Africa

indicators.note: the start of the word government is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A promising beginning for a new administration in an African state.
explanation.definitionFit: Benign can mean favourable or auspicious, as a propitious sign is.

clue.text: One reveres Ireland's foremost injured soldier

indicators.note: the foremost letter of the country's name is its first
injured letters are damaged and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone worships the first Irish soldier wounded in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' scrambles SOLDIER after I to give IDOLSER plus I placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: An idoliser is someone who worships or venerates another, as one who reveres does.
